Note::undefined¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

static Note Note::undefined() noexcept

Construct The Absence State¶

Note::undefined() constructs a Note handle with no backing value. It is the explicit absence state used when an operation has no Note to return or an optional Note argument has not been supplied. It is not a null text lane, not an empty string, and not a defined Note with a zero-sized dimension.

The distinction is structural. An undefined Note has no dtype or shape. The non-throwing probes report defined() == false, dim() == 0, numel() == 0, and empty() == true, but the zero dimension is only a safe fallback: the handle is not a scalar, and is_scalar() remains false. Queries that require an actual value, including dtype(), sizes(), and lane access, reject it.

Construction is constant-time, performs no allocation, and is noexcept. Copying or moving the handle preserves the undefined state. Many shape-preserving Note operations propagate undefined, while operations that require concrete data may reject it; use defined() before entering code whose absence behavior is not part of its contract.

Example 1: Absence And Empty Geometry Are Different¶

const auto absent = pluss::Note::undefined();
const auto empty = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<std::string>{}, std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 0});

std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "absent: defined=" << absent.defined()
          << " dim=" << absent.dim()
          << " numel=" << absent.numel()
          << " empty=" << absent.empty()
          << " scalar=" << absent.is_scalar() << '\n'
          << "empty: defined=" << empty.defined()
          << " dim=" << empty.dim()
          << " numel=" << empty.numel()
          << " empty=" << empty.empty()
          << " shape=[" << empty.size(0) << ", " << empty.size(1) << "]\n";

Output¶

absent: defined=false dim=0 numel=0 empty=true scalar=false
empty: defined=true dim=2 numel=0 empty=true shape=[2, 0]

Both are empty in the cardinality sense, but only the second carries valid Text dtype and rank-2 geometry.

Example 2: Dtype Access Requires A Defined Value¶

try {
  (void)pluss::Note::undefined().dtype();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "undefined dtype: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

undefined dtype: rejected

Check defined() before requesting metadata that cannot exist without storage.

Example 3: Copying Preserves Absence¶

const auto absent = pluss::Note::undefined();
const auto copied = absent;
std::cout << std::boolalpha << "copied defined=" << copied.defined() << '\n';

Output¶

copied defined=false

No placeholder allocation is introduced by the copy.

Example 4: Absence Survives A Binary Round Trip¶

const auto restored = pluss::note::unpack(pluss::Note::undefined().pack());
std::cout << std::boolalpha << "defined=" << restored.defined() << '\n';

Output¶

defined=false

The stable Note envelope records definition state separately from dtype and payload.

See Also¶

  • defined: test for this state without throwing.

  • empty: test element count, which also reports true for undefined.

  • pack: preserve undefined across a byte-oriented boundary.
